aegworldwide-aegworldwide:greenhouse:861.description: Company Information For more than 20 years, AEG has played a pivotal role in transforming sports and live entertainment. Annually, we host more than 160 million guests, promote more than 10,000 shows and present more than 22,000 events around the world. We are committed to innovation, artistry, and community, and leverage the power of our 300+ venues, leading sports franchises, marquee music brands, integrated entertainment districts, premier ticketing platform and global sponsorship activations, to create memorable moments that give the world reason to cheer. Our business is interwoven with the human mind and heart, and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive company that reflects the artists, athletes, and fans that we host; reach beyond traditional boundaries to support the communities in which we operate; and minimize our impact on the environment by adopting sustainable practices throughout our business operations. If you want to be challenged to up your game and make a difference, then join us in giving the world reason to cheer! JOB DESCRIPTION: AEG and the Ontario Reign are looking for talented individuals to join their game- day production team. All Game Day Camera Operators will be a part of the Reign’s AHLTV broadcast team, through filming live game action, as well as the Reign’s overall content creation team. Footage from Camera Operators will be used live on the Reign’s AHLTV broadcast, as well as in postgame highlight packages and other Ontario Reign video segments and marketing materials, including those featured on social media, ontarioreign.com and other affiliated outlets. This position is a game-day only position and will be compensated hourly. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Film live, hockey action at the instruction of the Production Director. Camera operators must be able to creatively frame and capture live action, take direction from the production director and seamlessly transition between different shots to create a high-quality, professional online broadcast Responsible for filming live game action from both tight and wide camera roles, detailed player shots, crowd shots and any other footage as directed by the Production Director Troubleshooting - resolve technical or practical issues as they arise, such as shot focus, shot framing, shot impairment, camera malfunction, or other, on- the-go issues that may arise during a live production, plus an ability to take direction on correcting these issues on the fly Equipment preparation/maintenance - prepare cameras and test angles or camera movements and ability to test, clean and maintain camera equipment, under the supervision of the production director SPECIFIC JOB KNOWLEDGE, SKILL AND ABILITY: The Camera Operator must possess the following knowledge, skills and abilities and be able to explain and demonstrate that he or she can perform the essential functions of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation, using some other combination of skill and abilities: Must be eager to create unique camera shots, have excellent communication with Director and production team and understand the basics of filming, exposure, focusing and composition Working knowledge of film equipment preferred, including ability to assemble and position equipment (cameras, tripods, etc.) Must have a flexible schedule including a willingness to work nights, weekends and holidays as applicable with the Reign’s home schedule Must be comfortable working in a fast paced, high-pressure environment Able to attend most, if not all, home Reign games and arrive two hours before game time for each game. QUALIFICATION STANDARDS: Education: High School Diploma or its equivalency Experience: A minimum of 2-4 years of related experience Past experience working on a live-sports production is preferred, particularly experience shooting with DSLR's and HD/live streaming camcorders Pay Scale: $16.90/hr Bonus: This position is not eligible for a bonus under the current bonus plan requirements. jobgether-jobgether:lever:22fd3269-05ae-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Experienced Electrical Technical Field Advisor based in the United States. This is a field-based technical leadership opportunity supporting the installation, commissioning, operation, and troubleshooting of electrical systems for gas and steam turbine equipment. You will serve as a technical authority during power generation projects, outages, and commissioning activities. The role combines hands-on electrical expertise with planning, problem-solving, documentation, and coordination of field resources. You’ll work closely with customers, plant owners, construction teams, and internal stakeholders to keep complex assignments on track. The position requires strong knowledge of excitation systems, turbine controls, generators, digital and analog controls, and associated software. Frequent travel, including offshore assignments, is an integral part of the role, with flexibility required for weekends, holidays, and overtime. This is an opportunity to apply your engineering judgment in critical energy infrastructure environments while contributing directly to safe, reliable power generation. Install, commission, operate, and troubleshoot generator excitation systems, digital electronic starters (LCI), generator protection systems, and associated wiring for gas and steam turbines. Configure, modify, and troubleshoot hardware and software associated with turbine and generator control systems. Trace and interpret software documentation, modify control constants, and adjust software sequencing as required to support system performance. Implement excitation control system software changes and work with both legacy and modern operator interfaces, including DOS- and Windows NT-based systems. Apply knowledge of analog and digital controls, control logic, PLCs, instrumentation, and turbine auxiliary systems to diagnose and resolve technical issues. Provide technical direction for electrical wiring installation and termination, complete functionality checks, and troubleshoot turbine excitation and LCI systems. Perform and support turbine and generator start-up and shutdown sequencing , ensuring systems operate according to technical and contractual requirements. Review plant engineering documentation, including P&IDs and related technical materials, to understand system configurations and support field execution. Plan and coordinate pre-outage activities, installations, and field work, including labor, tools, materials, equipment, and other required resources. Support control of project costs, quality, equipment preservation, security, and safekeeping of turbine modules, tools, spare parts, trailers, cranes, and related assets. Provide clear technical updates and progress reports to customers, plant or utility owners, construction organizations, and other stakeholders as required. Develop or recommend field policies and procedures and proactively support continuous improvements in execution and operational practices. Collaborate effectively with field personnel, customers, and project teams while using sound judgment to resolve issues and keep assignments progressing. Travel frequently and work on offshore assignments when required, with flexibility to work weekends, holidays, and overtime based on field schedules. Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering with at least 3 years of relevant experience, or at least 5 years of relevant experience without a formal degree. Relevant experience should include power plant maintenance, turbine generator maintenance, power plant equipment installation, commissioning, or closely related field engineering work . Successful completion of all required technical and company training programs is mandatory. Demonstrated experience successfully supporting power plant installations and outages , with the ability to operate independently while knowing when and where to seek add

sierrastudio-sierra-studio:ashbyhq:35974.title: Entrepreneur in Residence (EIR)
sierrastudio-sierra-studio:ashbyhq:35974.description: 🧑‍🚀 JOB TITLE: ENTREPRENEUR IN RESIDENCE (EIR) Location: United States (flexible) or Brazil Employment Type: Full Time Location Type: Remote Department: Sierra – EIR Compensation: Cash & Equity 🏔️ ABOUT SIERRA STUDIO Sierra is an AI First engineering studio and tech incubator. We turn our customers’ ideas into reality! We’re based in Los Angeles, but our teammates live all around the world. We do everything with an AI First approach, including coding, building our own tooling, and exploring incubating ideas that get traction internally. 💼 ABOUT THE ROLE An EIR is somebody who wants to start their own company and is actively experimenting to prepare. The idea of an EIR has existed for a while. Mostly in the context of the venture studio model, in which traditional VC is combined with some sort of talent program to incubate businesses. Our version of the role is slightly different. Sierra is a talent focused organization, but Sierra is self funded through revenue and not the traditional VC model. Our advantage is our team and the understanding we gain while building. Our engineering & hiring services work is a unique opportunity to explore different domains and technologies in a short time to inspire your future startup’s vision. Sierra EIRs are responsible for leading client projects AND encouraged to start a new business leveraging our resources & ecosystem. EIRs are also involved with building our company AI First. Our environment uniquely evolves our people’s understanding, ideas, and skills to build next-gen companies. 🧠 WHAT MAKES A GREAT EIR? We’re looking for entrepreneurial minds with a bias to action and a systems-thinking lens. You might be an engineer, a product thinker, or a domain expert who’s felt the itch to build something of your own. 🧬 Core Skills - High curiosity and fast learning ability - Strong systems thinking - Clear communicator across ideas and execution - Emotionally intelligent and low ego - Background in engineering, product, or an industry domain - Deep understanding of (or excitement about) AI-first thinking 🎁 Bonus Points - Strong product sense or design chops - Solid coding or architecture experience - Experience with ML, LLMs, or data science - A personal brand or strong professional network - Experience as a 2nd+ time founder 🔧 DAY IN THE LIFE OF AN EIR If you’re coming from a product or engineering background, this version of the EIR experience is for you. It’s geared toward builders who think in systems, tools, and products. Through client work and internal initiatives, you’ll: - Gain rapid exposure to a variety of domains and technologies - Identify recurring patterns and unmet needs across industries - Develop Sierra’s internal AI Roadmap (internal tools, research, experiments) - Contribute to the design and iteration of early-stage AI products Over time, you’ll chart your own path: - 🚀 Found a new company - 🤝 Join another Sierra incubation as a co-founder - 🧭 Step into a technical leadership role within Sierra 🌱 WHAT ARE THE OUTCOMES OF BECOMING AN EIR? As an EIR, many of the fundamental pain points are removed from the early days of starting a company: - You don’t have to stealthily moonlight your startup while juggling another job to pay the bills. - Your entrepreneurship is institutionally encouraged and fostered. - You work with a high-agency and low-ego team of potential co-founders / founding engineers. - You can openly collaborate on your incubation and use our environment as a playground to explore new ideas. - You work in a system that is rapidly surfacing needs, roadmapping, and iterating on new AI tools/products. - You serve our clients and company. You grow and learn faster than you have before. After some time, you found your own company, and Sierra does everything we can to set up a great team and support your journey.
